clue.text: It's the M.O's turn, possibly, for a remedy

indicators.note: possibly says the letters of the M.O's turn may be arranged some other way

parts.note: the letters M, O and S taken as printed, with the apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: A doctor says it is the medical officer's turn to prescribe a remedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges MOS plus TURN. A nostrum is a quack remedy.
explanation.definitionFit: A nostrum is a pet cure or quack medicine, a kind of remedy.

clue.text: A head for drink

explanation.surface: Someone with a good capacity for alcohol.
explanation.definitionFit: Noggin is slang for the skull and also an old small measure of liquor, a gill.

clue.text: Quietly painstaking

parts.note: read 'painstaking' as taking pain, and quietly: bearing suffering without complaint

explanation.surface: A description of a diligent, unassuming worker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'painstaking' looks like careful work, but split it as pains-taking: someone who takes pain without a murmur.
explanation.definitionFit: A Stoic philosopher endured hardship calmly, so the adjective means bearing pain silently.

clue.text: Making new entrances into the world?

definitions.text: Making new entrances into the world?

parts.words: Making new entrances into the world?
parts.note: entering the world anew is being born again, so the clue describes rebirth or revival

explanation.surface: Debutantes making their first appearances in society.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means being reborn or springing up afresh, a second entry into life.

clue.text: Maybe no man is a mug to be generous!

indicators.note: maybe signals that the phrase no man is a mug could be rearranged

explanation.surface: A remark that being generous doesn't make anyone a fool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maybe' rearranges the eleven letters of NO MAN IS A MUG.
explanation.definitionFit: Magnanimous means big-hearted and forgiving, freely giving to others.

clue.text: Sticks here in an island

indicators.note: in places the word here within the island's name

parts.note: Cos (Kos) is a Greek island in the Dodecanese
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone stuck here on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: The Greek island is usually spelt Kos today; crosswords keep the older spelling. 'Sticks' looks like a noun (twigs) but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To cohere is to hold together, to stick as one mass.

clue.text: One that starts catching small rodents

definitions.text: One that starts catching small rodents

indicators.note: the opening letters of the word catching are taken, its start

explanation.surface: A pet beginning its career as a mouser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starts' takes the first three letters of 'catching'; the whole clue also describes the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A cat is the classic mouser, a hunter of mice and other small rodents.

clue.text: Where can the cutter be?

indicators.note: can, with be, suggests the word where may become something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone asking where a missing cutting tool has gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can ... be' rearranges WHERE. A hewer cuts wood or coal.
explanation.definitionFit: A hewer is someone who chops, such as a miner cutting coal at the face.

clue.text: Tell one he celebrated

parts.note: Tell is the Swiss hero William Tell, whom this Italian composer celebrated in an opera

explanation.surface: An instruction to inform someone that he partied.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tell' looks like a verb but is William Tell, subject of the opera with the famous overture.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian composer wrote the opera William Tell, so he celebrated that hero in music.

clue.text: More of an eccentric than an acquaintance

definitions.text: More of an eccentric than an acquaintance

parts.words: More of an eccentric than an acquaintance
parts.note: two readings: more odd, the comparative of odd; and someone unknown, the opposite of an acquaintance

explanation.surface: A remark comparing a weird person with someone you know.
explanation.walkthrough: The comparative of 'strange' means more eccentric, and the noun is a person not known to you, the reverse of an acquaintance.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the comparative 'more odd' and a person one has never met.

clue.text: Farewell which Galahad heard as a compliment?

indicators.note: heard tells us the knightly description is taken by its sound

parts.note: Sir Galahad, the purest of King Arthur's knights, is the archetypal virtuous knight

explanation.surface: Arthur's knight mistaking a bedtime farewell for praise.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Galahad of Arthurian legend was the pure knight; the farewell sounds like praise of him.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is said as a parting at night, a form of farewell.

clue.text: Better informed by an old mariner for instance

definitions.text: Better informed by an old mariner for instance

parts.words: Better informed by an old mariner for instance
parts.note: in Coleridge's poem the Ancient Mariner's listener leaves sadder and more knowing

explanation.surface: Someone who has learned a thing or two from a retired sailor.
explanation.walkthrough: Coleridge's Rime of the Ancient Mariner ends with the Wedding Guest rising 'a sadder and a wiser man'.
explanation.definitionFit: Having learned from the tale, the listener is more knowing, better informed.

clue.text: What's a bone doing in a pincushion?

indicators.note: in tells us the bone's name sits within the letters of pincushion

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about a bone found stuck in a sewing cushion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' points to the run inside pINCUShion. The incus is the anvil bone of the middle ear.
explanation.definitionFit: The incus is one of the three tiny ossicles of the middle ear, a bone.

clue.text: Share out a bit, say

indicators.note: say signals that the phrase for a bit is taken as spoken

parts.note: a bit is a portion, giving the two words a portion

explanation.surface: An instruction to divide something up, a little at a time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' means the phrase 'a portion' is heard, sounding like the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To apportion is to divide and distribute in shares.

clue.text: Not a true map, perhaps, in one's baggage

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the letters of not a true map are rearranged

explanation.surface: A misleading map found tucked into one's luggage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges the eleven letters of NOT A TRUE MAP.
explanation.definitionFit: A portmanteau is a large travelling trunk that opens into two halves, a piece of luggage.

clue.text: No apparent cause of action

parts.note: a hidden reason behind someone's deed, not the one shown openly

explanation.surface: A lawyer saying a case has no obvious grounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cause of action' sounds like legal jargon, but it is a hidden reason for doing something.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a concealed reason for acting, as opposed to the stated one.

clue.text: Lack of light in one sort of camera

definitions.text: Lack of light in one sort of camera

parts.words: Lack of light in one sort of camera
parts.note: darkness, as in the darkened chamber of the camera obscura

explanation.surface: A photographer complaining of darkness in a camera.
explanation.walkthrough: The camera obscura (Latin 'dark chamber') projects images into a darkened room.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means darkness or dimness, the state of having no light.

clue.text: Immobile water carrier

parts.note: a structure that carries water but never moves, unlike a bucket or tanker

explanation.surface: A water bearer who refuses to move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carrier' suggests a person or vehicle, but this one is a fixed bridge-like channel.
explanation.definitionFit: An aqueduct is a fixed channel or bridge conveying water over distance.

clue.text: He is of a quizzical disposition

definitions.text: He is of a quizzical disposition

parts.words: He is of a quizzical disposition
parts.note: quizzical read as running a quiz: the person who asks the questions

explanation.surface: A description of a man inclined to raise an eyebrow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quizzical' usually means puzzled, but here it means given to quizzes.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the person who sets and puts the questions in a quiz.

clue.text: Making no headway in circulation

parts.note: water swirling round in circles without moving forward

explanation.surface: A newspaper failing to increase its readership.
explanation.walkthrough: 'circulation' suggests a newspaper's sales, but it is water going round in a whirl.
explanation.definitionFit: Eddying water whirls round in circles rather than flowing onward.

clue.text: No object in keeping on?

parts.note: object read as end or goal; with none, the thing goes on for ever

explanation.surface: Someone wondering whether there is any point continuing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'object' means an end or aim; without an end, a thing continues interminably.
explanation.definitionFit: Something without an end goes on for ever, ceaseless.

clue.text: Some held it to be self-evident in 1776

definitions.text: Some held it to be self-evident in 1776

parts.words: Some held it to be self-evident in 1776
parts.note: the American Declaration of Independence: 'We hold these ... to be self-evident'

explanation.surface: A historical remark about American revolutionaries.
explanation.walkthrough: The 1776 Declaration of Independence begins 'We hold these truths to be self-evident'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Declaration called certain facts self-evident, true statements beyond question.

clue.text: Principal boy?

parts.note: principal read as chief in line: the first-born male heir rather than a pantomime role

explanation.surface: A theatrical term for the hero of a pantomime.
explanation.walkthrough: In British pantomime the 'principal boy' is the hero, traditionally played by a woman; here it is the first-born son, chief heir.
explanation.definitionFit: The first-born male child is the chief heir, the main son of a family.

clue.text: This meat may be eaten by vegetarians

definitions.text: This meat may be eaten by vegetarians

parts.words: This meat may be eaten by vegetarians
parts.note: this word before meat makes a confection, so the 'meat' is candy

explanation.surface: A menu note about a meat that vegetarians may eat.
explanation.walkthrough: A sweetmeat is a sugary confection, no meat at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Joined to 'meat' it names a candy, which vegetarians may happily eat.

clue.text: As to this, it's in two parts below

definitions.text: As to this, it's in two parts

explanation.surface: A note that something lies split in two underneath.
explanation.walkthrough: Put AS before this word and it becomes 'asunder', meaning in two parts; on its own it means below.
explanation.definitionFit: Placing 'as' before it gives a word meaning split apart, and on its own it means beneath.

clue.text: Join (or separate by turning it round)

indicators.note: turning it round tells us the two letters of it are reversed within the word for separate

parts.note: to separate a knot is to undo it, to untie

explanation.surface: An instruction to connect things, or to part them by turning around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning it round' swaps the TI in UNTIE back to IT, and separating becomes joining.
explanation.definitionFit: To unite is to bring together into one, to join.

clue.text: No noisy occupant of a house in Columbia's district

definitions.text: No noisy occupant of a house in Columbia's district

parts.note: not noisy means quiet, and quiet is p, piano in music
someone living in a house is a resident

explanation.surface: A quiet tenant living in a house in Washington.
explanation.walkthrough: P is piano, quiet in music. The White House is in the District of Columbia, Washington.
explanation.definitionFit: The head of state of the USA lives in the White House in Washington DC.

clue.text: A writer's enclosure

parts.note: two senses: an instrument a writer uses, and a fenced area for animals

explanation.surface: An author's study or private retreat.
explanation.walkthrough: The word is both a writing implement and a small enclosure for animals.
explanation.definitionFit: It is both a writing tool and a fold for sheep or pigs.

clue.text: One way to remedy loose behaviour?

definitions.text: One way to remedy loose behaviour?

parts.words: One way to remedy loose behaviour?
parts.note: loose read literally, as slack, so the cure is to make it firmer

explanation.surface: A moralist's suggestion for dealing with promiscuity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loose behaviour' suggests immorality, but the cure is to make something less slack.
explanation.definitionFit: Making something firmer cures slackness, the literal sense of looseness.

clue.text: Classical globe-trotter

parts.note: the Latin name of the hero of Homer's Odyssey, who wandered for ten years

explanation.surface: A description of a well-travelled ancient hero.
explanation.walkthrough: This is the Latin name of Odysseus, whose ten-year voyage home is the Odyssey.
explanation.definitionFit: The Homeric hero wandered the known world for a decade, the archetypal traveller.
